pr_body:
##### SUMMARY

Fixes #82239

Adding a new role dir to the plugin loader clears the plugin loader cache, but the variable `cached_vars_plugin_order` in ansible.vars.plugins is never reset, preventing new plugins from being found.

Remove cache in the middle and use the vars plugin loader cache as the load-order. To make this possible, the cache keys now include non-stateless vars plugins (the value is a None, unresolved PluginLoadContext() tuple to be easily distinguished from stateless plugins).

### Summary

More specifically, I am using gekmihesg.openwrt to manage a number of OpenWRT routers (which do not have python support) using distro version(s) of ansible.

With upgrade to Fedora 39, I got ansible-core 2.16.0~rc1, release 1.fc39 which I suppose is something very close to the current development version. This version fails to pick up the openwrt vars_plugin at all, and I had limited luck in debugging what happens. Moving on to poetry install ansible instead, I notice I get 'ansible [core 2.15.6]' and everything works just fine (after I remove the exception I had introduced for debugging purposes..)

I experimented with various settings of this in ansible.cfg, but it did not change behaviour - the vars_plugins code under the gekmihesg.openwrt directory appears to never get called:

vars_plugins_enabled = ansible.builtin.host_group_vars,gekmihesg.openwrt

Anyway, whether I am configuring something wrong or need something extra w/version 2.16 was kind of frustrating to figure out so I thought you might want to know about it so that at least the documentation can be improved.

> Moving on to poetry install ansible instead, I notice I get 'ansible [core 2.15.6]' and everything works just fine (after I remove the exception I had introduced for debugging purposes..)

Note that ansible-core 2.15 does not support Fedora 39 and Python 3.12 which is why we have ansible-core-2.16.0~rc1 packaged (the Fedora 2.16.0 release build is also [coming down the pipe](https://bodhi.fedoraproject.org/updates/FEDORA-2023-0fec669bd8)).

> the vars_plugins code under the gekmihesg.openwrt directory appears to never get called

Are you sure the plugin is actually enabled and properly configured? Your `ansible-config dump --only-changed -t all` output does not show that it's enabled. If the vars plugin is indeed enabled, it's possible that whatever [brittle monkeypatching](https://github.com/gekmihesg/ansible-openwrt/blob/master/vars_plugins/monkeypatch.py) it's doing is not compatible with ansible-core 2.16. In that case, this bug should be reported to that project and not to ansible-core.

What would be good would be if the VARIABLE_PLUGINS_ENABLED variable was somehow checked. Maybe I am just using the wrong naming or otherwise miss something in the setup? It took me a while just to realize that I needed to also provide `ansible.builtin.host_group_vars` in the config setting, otherwise I would get a different, much earlier error.
And it is still not clear to me whether just `gekmihesg.openwrt` is the right way to reference the vars plugin since it really references a role and maybe not the plugin itself?

> If the vars plugin is indeed enabled, it's possible that whatever [brittle monkeypatching](https://github.com/gekmihesg/ansible-openwrt/blob/master/vars_plugins/monkeypatch.py) it's doing is not compatible with ansible-core 2.16. In that case, this bug should be reported to that project and not to ansible-core.

If the plugin gets enabled, I would expect the python code in the link would be evaluated, but no tricks I could think of (such as adding a breakpoint() or a syntax error in the plugin would yield any effect?

Besides that, I agree with the brittleness, and I believe so does the author, but apparently no good alternatives arised from the initial discussion around this. Is there a better approach to handle targets which cannot run python? The plugin has been really useful and blends in well with other (python supported) targets. I maintain another set of routers with custom built Linux images, there I have so far had to rely entirely on raw rules, a much less satisfactory solution. Anyway, this is maybe a separate topic.

First `gekmihesg.openwrt`  is just a collection name, not a valid reference to the plugin itself, much less to a plugin inside a role. 

The issue might stem from this bugfix #79945.  Which is now probably happening too soon for a vars plugin in a role to be loaded.

As for the monkey patch ... I would really just use the `openwrt_module` actions instead of tryinig to hijack and rename 'normal modules' ..specially since not all have a openwrt.sh version. Also, instead of a vars plugin, I would use an overriden `normal.py` action plugin to do so, would not even need a monkey patch, just rename the module before calling `_configure`.

Ansible already supports using 'non python modules' and even dealing with multple interpreters ( `ansible_perl_interpreter`, `ansible_bash_interpreter`, etc) , you can even 'hijack' the module names by just adding them to `library/` or `action_plugins/` (for things like copy and template), it does not support simple renaming in that way, you can kind of do it with collections, but that is not something i recommend.
A quick workaround would be to create an actual collection and move the vars plugin there, then you could reference it correctly in config (`myns.myopenwrt.monkeypatch`).
